sources.entry: SPIS - A simple, lightweight and fast media server with decent mobile support. GPL-3.0 Docker/Rust

summary.one_liner: SPIS is a lightweight, fast, self-hosted server for browsing images and videos stored on a private machine, with a mobile-friendly web UI.
summary.what_it_does: SPIS serves media files from a directory on your own server through a minimal web interface. It processes media (generating thumbnails) on a configurable schedule or at startup, and it can run on Docker or as a standalone binary behind a webserver such as nginx. The UI offers endless scrolling, favorites, slideshows, filtering by year, month, favorites, and subdirectories, and multi-select with long press. Users can define custom shell commands that run on the current media file and appear as buttons in the UI. Configuration comes from CLI flags, environment variables, or a TOML file, and the binary can render nginx, systemd, and docker-compose config templates. The README says the author runs it with about 40,000 images on a Raspberry Pi CM4.
use_cases: browse personal images and videos on a home server
view a large media library on a Raspberry Pi
share a media folder with family on phone
run custom scripts on photos from a web UI
how_to_run: Binary: download spis, install nginx, and optionally install ffmpeg/ffprobe for video support
notable: Designed to avoid databases and extra components; configuration is a single flag/env/TOML setup
Custom commands defined in config run scripts on the current file with {path} substitution and optional hotkeys
Built-in config templating renders nginx, systemd, and docker-compose files
Installable as a progressive web app on mobile and desktop
Never reads media through spis itself during browsing; the webserver serves files directly
caveats: Binary install requires a separate webserver such as nginx to serve media
Video support needs ffmpeg and ffprobe installed and on the PATH
Either a server address or a UNIX socket must be set, but not both
keywords: self-hosted alternative to photo management apps
